annotation: AI-authored and source-inspected; provisional page-level positive anchors, not exhaustive relevance judgements or independent expert labels. No source text used to train embeddings or reranker. All 50 cases are a development benchmark, not held-out generalization evidence.

cases.question: What is the advancing side in FSW?
cases.reference_answer: Tool rotation and welding travel have the same direction on the advancing side.

cases.question: What is the retreating side in FSW?
cases.reference_answer: Tool rotation opposes the welding travel direction on the retreating side.

cases.question: What is an FSW bobbin tool?
cases.reference_answer: A bobbin tool has two shoulders separated by a fixed or adjustable pin.

cases.question: What is dwell time at the start of an FSW weld?
cases.reference_answer: The interval after full tool depth and before tool travel starts.

cases.question: What is dwell time at the end of an FSW weld?
cases.reference_answer: The interval between stopping travel and beginning withdrawal of the rotating tool.

cases.question: What is tool rotation speed in FSW?
cases.reference_answer: Angular tool speed measured in revolutions per minute.

cases.question: What does the FSW tool shoulder contact?
cases.reference_answer: The shoulder contacts the surface of the parent material.

cases.question: Does the scope of ISO 25239-5 include friction stir spot welding?
cases.reference_answer: The bundled preview excludes friction stir spot welding and refers to the ISO 18785 series.

cases.question: How many satisfactory test welds does the bundled FSW quality preview require for reproducibility testing?
cases.reference_answer: At least three satisfactory welds must be made and documented.

cases.question: Which inspection methods does the FSW quality preview list after welding?
cases.reference_answer: It lists visual, non-destructive and destructive testing, dimensional checks and postweld-operation records.

cases.question: In friction stir welding, which part of the tool projects into the workpiece?
cases.reference_answer: The pin extends into the workpiece to make the weld.

cases.question: Why does the friction stir process hold the plates firmly against a support during plunging?
cases.reference_answer: The non-consumable tool plunges between rigidly clamped materials supported on a backing plate.

cases.question: When FSW equipment is relocated, what repeatability demonstration does the quality preview require?
cases.reference_answer: Reproducibility testing applies to moved stationary equipment and requires at least three satisfactory documented welds under a production WPS.

cases.question: Before FSW, what contamination should be removed from the parent material?
cases.reference_answer: The parent material must be sufficiently free of contaminants such as oil, grease and dirt in accordance with the WPS.

cases.question: Does friction stir welding join metal by melting it?
cases.reference_answer: FSW is a solid-state process: frictional heating softens material and the rotating tool stirs it into a joint.

cases.question: Why is a two-shouldered FSW tool described as self-reacting?
cases.reference_answer: Its shoulders maintain contact with the workpiece on opposite sides, with a fixed or adjustable probe separating them.

cases.question: What does the thick-section FSW thesis mean by thick material?
cases.reference_answer: That thesis defines thick section as greater than 20 mm and studies 50 mm aluminium alloys.

cases.question: Why should an FSW monitoring method be tested across different aluminium alloys?
cases.reference_answer: The monitoring paper identifies limited generalization of earlier studies to one alloy, thickness or parameter set.

cases.question: How were internal voids checked independently in the FSW force-monitoring study?
cases.reference_answer: Welds were inspected using micro-focus computed tomography.

cases.question: Which moving parts does the FSW handbook identify for thermal management?
cases.reference_answer: The thermal management system includes the tool and spindle connection, workpiece and backing anvil.

cases.question: What is the TMAZ?
cases.reference_answer: The thermomechanically affected zone is plastically deformed and altered by welding heat.

cases.question: What is the HAZ?
cases.reference_answer: The heat affected zone has microstructure or properties changed by heat without tool plastic deformation.

cases.question: What does axial force mean?
cases.reference_answer: It is force on the workpiece along the tool rotation axis.

cases.question: What is the anvil used for?
cases.reference_answer: The anvil supports the root side of the joint.

cases.question: What does travel speed measure?
cases.reference_answer: The rate at which the welding operation advances along the welding direction.

cases.question: Explain the shoulder scroll feature.
cases.reference_answer: A shoulder scroll can contain softened material and remove the need for tool tilt.

cases.question: What does dynamically recrystallized zone mean?
cases.reference_answer: The stir zone is also called the dynamically recrystallized zone or weld nugget.

cases.question: Why is the solid-state joining tool called non-consumable?
cases.reference_answer: The rotating shoulder and probe stir friction-softened parent material rather than supply filler.

cases.question: In FSW, compare the advancing and retreating sides and distinguish tool rotation speed from travel speed.
cases.reference_answer: Advancing rotation agrees with travel and retreating rotation opposes it; rotation speed is angular speed in RPM while travel speed is forward progress.

cases.question: In FSW, compare the definitions of HAZ and TMAZ.
cases.reference_answer: Heat affects the HAZ without tool plastic deformation; the TMAZ experiences both heat and tool plastic deformation.

cases.question: How do the FSW quality preview requirements differ before and after welding?
cases.reference_answer: Before welding the WPS governs preparation and cleaning; afterward selected inspections, tests and dimensional/postweld checks verify compliance.

cases.question: How does the FSW thesis connect marine applications with its thick-section study?
cases.reference_answer: FSW is used in shipbuilding; marine superstructures motivate thicker sections, and the thesis studies 50 mm alloys under its greater-than-20-mm definition.

cases.question: Why are FSW force signals studied, and how did the monitoring paper independently check internal defects?
cases.reference_answer: Force/torque variations offer indirect quality feedback while micro-focus CT was used to inspect internal defects.

cases.question: Compare a bobbin FSW tool with dual-rotation tooling.
cases.reference_answer: Bobbin tools have two shoulders separated by a pin; dual-rotation tooling independently rotates pin and shoulder.

cases.question: How is that different from the retreating side?
cases.reference_answer: Advancing-side rotation agrees with travel, while retreating-side rotation opposes it.
